title: INT8 calibration mesh adapter and inference fallbacks for prefetch-heavy transformers
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Large decoder-only transformer workloads with aggressive KV prefetching and long-lived sessions show inconsistent INT8 accuracy when using naive per-tensor scale calibration. SmoothQuant-style activation rebalancing helps but interacts poorly with our kernel selection and KV cache prefetch patterns, leading to tail-case SUT spikes and occasional +3-7% generation quality regression on specific prompts. Goal: implement a mesh-style calibration adapter that synthesizes per-layer and cross-layer activation scaling profiles at calibration time, publishes compatible INT8 kernels, and adds a lightweight runtime divergence detector with safe fallbacks (fp16/fp32 kernels or per-request dequantization) when production signals indicate degraded output quality or degraded likelihood calibration. This ticket covers the calibration mesh adapter, model profiling harness, compatibility matrix for kernels, and the runtime fallback orchestration.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Mesh adapter produces stable per-model calibration profiles for 90% of sampled prompts with delta perplexity <= 0.8% vs fp32 baseline on eval set; 2) Runtime divergence detector triggers fallback within 20ms of detection and end-to-end latency penalty <= 10% for fallback paths; 3) Automated CI validates kernel compatibility for top-5 transformer variants and publishes metrics to console dashboard; 4) Documentation and runbook added in Confluence with links to calibration artifacts and rollback steps.
comments: 2025-02-14 - Spike: ran calibration mesh on Llama-family small testset. Observed cross-layer rescaling reduces per-layer saturation by 18% and improved token-level logprobs on average. Baseline test harness in repo under experiments/mesh-adapter.

2025-02-18 - Design sync with runtime: agreed that kernel ABI should expose a validity-check hook that returns a numeric divergence score; runtime will call this hook after the first token batch and every N steps (configurable). If score > threshold, route request to fp16 kernel and emit alert metric. Marcus to own kernel shim PR.

2025-02-21 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/quantization/pull/1428 implements the mesh profile writer and a minimal runtime shim. Initial CI failing on a mismatch in KV cache layout for 2D fused kernels. Investigating whether prefetch offsets differ with activation rebalancing.

2025-02-24 - Profiling: ran 1200 synthetic chats with KV prefetch enabled. Found a 6% tail latency increase in INT8 path for sequence lengths >1024; traced to additional memory ops in fused kernel. Workaround: introduce a per-model kernel preference where models with avg seq_len>800 default to fp16 unless expected cost reduction > 1.8x.

2025-02-28 - Experiment results: On our 10k prompt eval set (mix of short/long context), mesh-adapted INT8 achieves mean perplexity delta +0.4% and median latency -22% vs fp32. For the 2% worst prompts, divergence detector flagged 95% and fallback prevented quality regression. Metrics pushed to Grafana dashboard (see artifacts).

2025-03-03 - Blocker discovered: on a customer's long-conversation workload using streaming + tool-calls, fallback path caused subtle ordering regression in streaming chunks due to mixer logic assuming INT8 KV layout. Mitigation: add layout-compat shim in runtime to normalize the stream chunker. Engineering estimate +2 days.
